title: Gaming & VR Privacy Hardening Checklist
metaDescription: Complete privacy checklist for gamers and VR users. Secure your gaming platforms, protect personal data, and prevent tracking across devices.
intro: Gaming platforms and VR headsets collect vast amounts of personal data, from biometric information to voice recordings. This checklist helps you secure your gaming privacy across all platforms and devices, protecting your personal information while maintaining your gaming experience.

items.task: Configure Steam privacy settings
items.why: Steam collects gameplay data, purchase history, and social interactions that can reveal personal patterns and preferences.
items.howTo: Go to Steam > Settings > Privacy. Set profile to 'Friends Only' or 'Private'. Disable game details sharing, inventory display, and friend activity notifications. Turn off data collection for Steam Labs.

items.task: Disable Xbox telemetry and data sharing
items.why: Xbox collects detailed gameplay analytics, voice commands, and behavioral data for advertising and game improvement.
items.howTo: In Xbox settings, go to Privacy & Online Safety > Xbox Privacy. Set to 'Blocked' for: others can see your real name, game clips, screenshots. Disable optional diagnostic data sharing.

items.task: Limit PlayStation data collection
items.why: PlayStation Network tracks gaming habits, purchases, and social interactions for targeted advertising and analytics.
items.howTo: Settings > Account Management > Privacy Settings. Restrict profile visibility, disable activity feeds, turn off personalized ads. Disable automatic screenshot sharing and gameplay recording.

items.task: Secure Nintendo Switch privacy controls
items.why: Nintendo collects play activity data and can share information with game developers and advertising partners.
items.howTo: System Settings > Users > Privacy Settings. Disable 'Display play activity to others'. Turn off screenshot/video sharing to social media. Restrict friend suggestions and discovery.

items.task: Configure Epic Games privacy settings
items.why: Epic Games shares data with third parties and uses extensive analytics for advertising and platform improvement.
items.howTo: Account settings > Privacy. Disable public profile, friend requests from non-friends. Turn off data sharing for advertising. Disable cross-platform play data sharing if not needed.

items.task: Audit and clean up old gaming accounts
items.why: Unused gaming accounts remain vulnerable to breaches and continue collecting data even when inactive.
items.howTo: List all gaming platforms you've used. Delete unused accounts or set them to maximum privacy. Remove payment methods from inactive accounts. Update passwords on active accounts.

items.task: Disable VR biometric data collection
items.why: VR headsets collect sensitive biometric data including eye tracking, facial expressions, and movement patterns that create unique digital fingerprints.
items.howTo: In VR settings, disable eye tracking for advertising, facial recognition features, and movement analytics. Turn off data sharing with app developers. Regularly clear stored biometric profiles.

items.task: Limit Meta/Oculus data integration
items.why: Meta integrates VR data with Facebook profiles for advertising and social features, creating comprehensive behavioral profiles.
items.howTo: Oculus app > Settings > Privacy. Disable social features linking, advertising personalization, and data sharing with Facebook. Use separate accounts if possible.

items.task: Disable VR voice recording and processing
items.why: VR platforms record voice commands and conversations, which can be stored and analyzed for various purposes.
items.howTo: Turn off voice commands, voice chat recording, and speech-to-text features in VR settings. Disable always-listening microphone features. Mute mic when not needed.

items.task: Limit VR room scanning and mapping
items.why: Room mapping data reveals your living space layout and can be combined with other data for detailed profiling.
items.howTo: Use minimal room setup options. Disable room data sharing with developers. Regularly clear stored room maps. Use privacy screens when possible during setup.

items.task: Review VR app permissions and data access
items.why: VR apps often request excessive permissions to access personal data, camera, microphone, and system information.
items.howTo: Review each VR app's permissions in headset settings. Deny unnecessary access to camera, microphone, storage, and personal data. Uninstall apps you don't actively use.

items.task: Secure gaming voice chat settings
items.why: Voice chat is often recorded and can be analyzed for content, stored indefinitely, and shared with third parties.
items.howTo: Use push-to-talk instead of open mic. Disable voice chat recording in game settings. Use external voice apps like Discord with privacy settings enabled. Avoid sharing personal information in voice chat.

items.task: Create privacy-focused gaming usernames
items.why: Gaming usernames linked to real identity can be tracked across platforms and used to build comprehensive profiles.
items.howTo: Use unique usernames unrelated to real name or other online accounts. Avoid birth years, locations, or personal interests. Change usernames periodically if platforms allow.

items.task: Restrict gaming friend requests and social features
items.why: Open friend systems can expose you to harassment, doxxing, and unwanted contact from strangers.
items.howTo: Set friend requests to 'friends of friends' or manual approval only. Disable location sharing with friends. Turn off automatic game invitations and activity sharing.

items.task: Manage in-game chat history and logs
items.why: Chat logs are stored by gaming platforms and can be analyzed, subpoenaed, or accessed during data breaches.
items.howTo: Regularly clear chat history where possible. Disable chat logging in game settings. Avoid sharing sensitive information in game chats. Use temporary/disappearing message features when available.

items.task: Configure game streaming privacy settings
items.why: Game streaming can expose personal information visible on screen, voice, and gaming habits to large audiences.
items.howTo: Use streaming software privacy filters to hide personal information. Set up separate gaming profiles for streaming. Disable notifications during streams. Use a privacy-focused browser for any web browsing during streams.

items.task: Set up VPN for gaming privacy
items.why: Gaming without VPN exposes your real IP address to other players and gaming platforms, enabling tracking and potential DDoS attacks.
items.howTo: Choose a gaming-optimized VPN with low latency. Connect to nearby servers to minimize lag. Enable VPN kill switch to prevent IP leaks. Test gaming performance with VPN enabled.

items.task: Secure home router for gaming
items.why: Unsecured home networks expose all gaming traffic and can be exploited by attackers to access gaming accounts and personal data.
items.howTo: Change default router passwords. Enable WPA3 encryption. Disable WPS and unnecessary services. Set up guest network for gaming devices. Update router firmware regularly.

items.task: Keep gaming devices and software updated
items.why: Outdated gaming software contains security vulnerabilities that can be exploited to access personal data and accounts.
items.howTo: Enable automatic updates for gaming consoles, VR headsets, and PC gaming software. Regularly check for firmware updates. Update game clients and launchers promptly.

items.task: Secure gaming payment methods and purchases
items.why: Stored payment information in gaming accounts is a high-value target for attackers and can lead to unauthorized purchases.
items.howTo: Remove stored payment methods from gaming accounts. Use prepaid cards or digital wallets instead of credit cards. Enable purchase confirmations and spending limits. Monitor gaming-related charges regularly.

items.task: Use secure browser for gaming-related browsing
items.why: Gaming websites and forums often contain malware and tracking that can compromise gaming accounts and personal data.
items.howTo: Use a privacy-focused browser for gaming-related web browsing. Enable ad blockers and anti-tracking extensions. Avoid downloading game mods or cheats from untrusted sources. Clear browser data regularly.

pro_tips: Create separate email addresses for gaming accounts to isolate gaming data from personal communications and reduce tracking across services.
Use gaming-specific VPN servers optimized for low latency to maintain privacy without sacrificing gaming performance or competitive advantage.
Regularly review and delete old game recordings, screenshots, and clips that might contain personal information visible in the background.
Enable two-factor authentication on all gaming accounts, but avoid SMS-based 2FA due to SIM swapping risks - use authenticator apps instead.
Consider using a dedicated gaming device or partition to isolate gaming activities from personal computing and reduce cross-contamination of data.
